Subject: Renewal discussion & pricing ask

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for a great partnership this past year. We're kicking off renewal planning for our AI platform usage and wanted to flag two priorities up front: 1) a temporary price hold on base generation rates through the first half of the renewal term (Q3–Q4) to help us model the budget, and 2) a capacity uplift — we expect steady growth and need to secure more reserved capacity with predictable burst pricing.

We also saw a large unplanned overage in Q4 related to a product launch and would like to request a one-time operational credit to offset part of that spike. Procurement would like to see a concrete proposal that includes: committed volume options, discounts by tier, any credits you can offer, and how a price hold would be operationalized.

Attached: Atlas_Renewal_Report_Q4.pdf (summary usage + variances). Our procurement timeline is tight — ideally a signed amendment by mid-April. Can you put together options and a time to sync next week?

Best,
Sara Li
Head of Cloud Operations
AtlasHealth

Hi Sara — thanks for the context and the report. Looping in Karthik (pricing lead) and Lauren (CS) so we can put a concrete set of options in front of procurement quickly.

High-level, we can move on two tracks depending on how Atlas wants to balance price vs. long-term commitment:

Option A — 12-month renewal (preferred for flexibility)
- 10% off list generation rate on committed baseline
- $50,000 one-time operational credit to offset Q4 spike
- Price hold on baseline generation rate for first 6 months of the renewal (we'll lock the committed unit price; overage rates remain variable)
- Capacity uplift: reserve 1.5x current baseline with burst pool at fixed rate of $0.09/token-equivalent for bursts beyond reserved capacity

Option B — 24-month renewal (cost efficiency)
- 12% off list generation rate
- $100,000 one-time credit applied across first two invoices
- Grandfather base rate for full 12 months and then step-adjust by CPI index thereafter
- Capacity uplift: reserve 1.7x baseline, lower burst rate $0.07/token-equivalent

We need two things to refine: monthly consumption distribution (so Karthik can model true-unit economics across sequence lengths) and confirmation of whether procurement needs a formal LOI or signature-ready amendment. Lauren — can you confirm service continuity and SLO asks (anything over baseline we need to bake into SLA)?

I can do a 30-min call Thursday or Friday. If you can share a preferred cadence and the procurement doc you referenced, we'll prepare a detailed worksheet and a redline-ready amendment.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa,

Thanks — that framing is helpful. A few quick clarifications from procurement and ops:

- The $50k credit in Option A is a good start, but given the magnitude of the Q4 spike we're hoping for $75k on that path.
- For capacity uplift, we can't commit to 1.5x baseline immediately — finance prefers a 1.2x committed baseline for year one with a scheduled review at Q3 to potentially expand. We'd still like a defined burst pool and a predictable capped burst rate.
- For price hold implementation, procurement specifically asked whether the price hold can apply to both the base committed rate and the first 3 months of burst pricing (to smooth the immediate launch). If that's not possible, can Redwood provide a transitional burst-rate cap?
- Timeline: procurement can sign an amendment by April 22 if terms are finalized by April 16. Attached: Atlas_Procurement_Timeline.xlsx.

Can Karthik run the model again with (A) $75k credit + 1.2x committed uplift and (B) 24-month with $100k credit — also show monthly cashflow and expected invoice cadence.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Warm regards,
Sara

Hi Sara — thank you. I've updated the modeling and attached a formal proposal and two redline artifacts for procurement to review. Summary of the updated offer below.

Final Proposal (based on your feedback):

Path 1 (12-month, quicker execution):
- 10% discount on committed baseline generation rate
- One-time credit: $75,000 applied to first two invoices
- Committed baseline uplift: 1.2x current baseline for year one (scheduled Q3 review)
- Price hold: lock committed baseline unit price for the first 6 months of the renewal; for burst activity, offer a capped transitional burst rate of $0.085/token-equivalent for the first 3 months, then revert to standard burst tiers thereafter
- Delivery: signature-ready amendment + SOW to be shared; invoice cadence monthly in arrears

Path 2 (24-month, cost-forward):
- 12% discount on committed baseline generation rate
- One-time credit: $100,000 applied across the first three invoices
- Committed baseline uplift: 1.4x baseline (we can step to 1.6x in year 2 with review)
- Price hold: grandfather baseline rate for first 12 months; burst cap at $0.075/token-equivalent first 6 months

Conditional executive concession: I have approval to increase the one-time credit by an additional $25,000 (total $100k on Path 1) if Atlas executes the amendment by EOD 2027-04-16 and accepts our standard amendment template with the attached SOW. This is a time-limited concession tied to operational forecasting.

Attachments: Atlas_Pricing_Proposal_v3.xlsx (detailed tier model), SOW_draft.docx (workstream & onboarding timeline).

Next steps: Marissa will request the executive OK for the conditional concession and share the amendment/LOI for signature. Sara — if procurement is comfortable, we can target April 16 for commitment to secure the expanded credit. Please confirm any additional contract language procurement needs (data residency, audit window, or KMS specifics) so we can pre-bake it.
